note: Block A tasks that come from no screen or operation, so the slice cannot derive them. Read by tools/build-service-docs.py. Edit this file, not the task sheet. Added 30 September 2026 from the system-design review (audit/ticvai/steps/SD, findings SD-016, 024, 026, 028, 030-032, 034, 046-049, 051, 057, 059, 063) and the AI functions review (docs/active/ai-functions-review-30-september.md). `pool: backend` goes to the least-loaded backend owner; `assignee` names a person. AI engine tasks carry no points: they are sized in engineer-days in their text and planned by the two AI engineers, whose capacity is separate from the developers' (decided 30 September). Since 1 October a task may carry `block` (for example `B1`): it is recorded here with the ADR that asks for it and is not ticketed in the Block A sheet; build-service-docs.py skips it until that block is planned. A task without `block` is Block A. Since 1 October (the sprint plan) a later-block task names the app-module it lands in with `module` (a business module) and `platform` (P01-P17; none = that module's platform work), and build-service-docs.py plans it with the rest of the package. **The Block A AI chain split across both AI engineers** (Chinmay, 1 October): the baseline layer (estimators, venue profile, starting patterns) and Qdrant tenancy do not call the LLM gateway, so they start on day one beside it; day-one suggestions and the evaluation harness still wait for the gateway (an answer is recorded through its decision point), and the concierge for Qdrant. Kalpita Mejari: gateway, concierge, Help me choose, translations, planner (33 days); the second AI engineer: baseline, Qdrant, suggestions, evaluation (33 days). `appModule: baseline` puts a task in the second AI engine app-module of Block A, so each engineer's module test is of the other's half.

epics.subject: Platform kernel: tenant routing, scope, idempotency, outbox, payments, audit, observability
epics.detail: The machinery every service stands on and no screen asks for. Found missing by the system-design review of 29 September (SD-063, SD-047). Sprint 1 target: one web purchase and one offline POS cash sale end to end by 23 October.

epics.subject: Offline-first: journal, signed bundles, leases, sync, POS to kitchen
epics.detail: What the POS, the Kitchen Display and the scanner need to keep trading with the network down (SD-047, SD-028, SD-046, SD-052).

epics.subject: AI engine: Block A (gateway, baseline layer, concierge, Help me choose, translations, planner agent)
epics.detail: Built by the two AI engineers from 5 October (decided 30 September). Every AI answer works on day one from a baseline and learns from the tenant's own data; a trained model replaces the baseline only when it beats it and an admin approves (AI-D16). The AI endpoints and screens are built by the developers under their own tickets.

tasks.subject: Request kernel: hostname to tenant routing, per-transaction scope, error model and 429
tasks.detail: In ticvai-backend. Resolve the tenant from the hostname (control-plane routing table, SD-021), open every transaction with the tenant and scope settings the row-level policies read (SD-059), one problem-details error model, and 429 with Retry-After on the hot public operations (SD-043). Done when: two seeded tenants on two hostnames cannot read each other's rows, and a flood test returns 429 instead of 500.

tasks.subject: Durable idempotency: the Idempotency-Key store and middleware
tasks.detail: Idempotency records in PostgreSQL with Redis as a cache only (SD-024), so a retried payment or sale after a restart returns the first answer. Done when: replaying a createOrder with the same key after a service restart returns the original response and creates nothing.

tasks.subject: Outbox, relay and inbox behind the kernel broker interface, on a local RabbitMQ
tasks.detail: The transactional outbox per tenant database; one relay per region in the workers host, with a lease and a polling loop per tenant database, and an inbox per tenant database for exactly-once handling (ADR-0058); modules enqueue through IOutbox inside their own transaction, the relay publishes through IBrokerPublisher and consumers subscribe through IEventSubscriber (ADR-0058 amendment, 1 October); the relay drains a full batch at once and its batch size is configuration (Relay:BatchSize, 1,000 in the flash-sale environment). The broker per ADR-0057 is the client's choice between RabbitMQ and Kafka: build behind the kernel interface on a local RabbitMQ until they answer, with ordering per aggregate by an ordering key and dead letters drained into platform.dead_letter. A relay-lag dashboard and alert per tenant database (SD-030, SD-031, SD-032). Done when: an event written in a transaction reaches its consumer once, survives a relay restart and a redelivery, a poison message lands in platform.dead_letter, and relay lag shows on the dashboard and alerts when unpublished rows are older than 60 seconds.

tasks.subject: Republish from the outbox by tenant and time range
tasks.detail: The recovery path for a lost broker (ADR-0058 amendment, 1 October; the DR design in ADR-0060 relies on it): republishOutbox, listOutboxRepublishes, getOutboxRepublish and cancelOutboxRepublish in the operations host, carried out by the relay in workers with a keyset cursor over the outbox, published_at left untouched and live batches first; one job per tenant (control.outbox_republish). Done when: after a simulated broker loss, a republish of one tenant's last hour redelivers every event once to each consumer, the inbox drops the duplicates, and a second request for the same tenant while one runs is refused with 409.

tasks.subject: Order paid to tickets issued: the saga proven end to end
tasks.detail: order.paid consumed by the entitlement owner, tickets issued, the ledger posting once from the event, and holds converted with capacity decremented (SD-026, SD-023). Done when: a web purchase in the sandbox ends with a ticket, one ledger posting and sold capacity reduced, and a replayed event changes nothing.

tasks.subject: Payment adapter and signed webhook against the provider's test mode
tasks.detail: The provider adapter, the inbound signed webhook, the provider reference on payments, 3-D Secure redirect states and the card-terminal flow for the POS (SD-034). Done when: an approved, a declined and a 3-D Secure payment each end in the right order state from the webhook alone, with polling only as the fallback. Acceptance of the declined, unknown and reconcile paths waits on the client's payment sandbox credentials: see the client's answer in the Decisions Register.

tasks.subject: Audit interceptor for every write
tasks.detail: Who, what, when, tenant and venue for every write, written once by an interceptor rather than per operation (SD-057). Done when: any write in the Block A slice leaves one audit row a support user can read.

tasks.subject: Release flags per tenant
tasks.detail: Half-built features stay dark per tenant between sprints (SD-051). Done when: a flag switched off for one tenant hides a screen and refuses its operations for that tenant only.

tasks.subject: Row-level policies without a per-row subquery on hot tables
tasks.detail: Scope predicates read session settings instead of joining per row (SD-016). Done when: the order and scan-event queries keep their plan with policies on, measured on the seed data.

tasks.subject: Observability with tenant and venue on every trace, and the first dashboards
tasks.detail: OpenTelemetry attributes for tenant, venue and workstation; dashboards for the sale path and sync; alerts on error rate and latency (SD-048). Done when: a failed POS sale can be found by venue and till within a minute.

tasks.subject: Migration fan-out across tenant databases, and expand-then-contract changes
tasks.detail: Apply a migration to every tenant database with progress and resume, and the rule that a schema change ships in two steps so old and new code both run (SD-049). Done when: a column rename reaches three seeded tenant databases with no downtime.

tasks.subject: Hosts for the deployables on .NET 10: commerce, access, operations and workers, each composing its modules
tasks.detail: In **ticvai-backend**, on .NET 10 LTS (decided 30 September; ADR-0055). Four .NET hosts in one solution: commerce (Identity, Tenancy, Catalogue, Order, Ledger, Wallet), access (Access), operations (F&B, Retail, Inventory, VenueOps, Marketing, WhiteLabel, Reporting, Platform, CrossRegion) and workers (the outbox relay, every module's event consumers, scheduled jobs), each composing its modules through IModule. ticvai-ai stays the Python service. Done when: each host starts locally with its modules registered and a health endpoint, CI builds one image per host, and moving a module to another host is a change of one registration.

tasks.subject: Architecture tests for 17 modules: no module references another, and no module's SQL names another's schema
tasks.detail: Extend tests/Ticvai.ArchitectureTests/ModuleBoundaryTests.cs from six modules to 17 (ADR-0055), and add a test that fails when a module's SQL names another module's schema other than through a published read view. Done when: a deliberate cross-module reference and a raw cross-schema query each fail the build in CI.

tasks.subject: Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage
tasks.detail: A deriver reads handoff/api-data-lineage.json and generates, per owning module, the views other modules may read (894 cross-schema reads on 30 September; ADR-0055), applied by the migrations. Done when: every cross-schema read in the Block A slice goes through a published view, the views regenerate with one command, and a raw cross-schema read is reported by the lineage check.

tasks.subject: One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only
tasks.detail: Roles for commerce, access, operations, ticvai-ai and workers (ADR-0055), created in the baseline migrations and granted their modules' schemas plus the published read views; the ticvai-ai role is read-only on the transactional schemas (ADR-0020). Done when: each host connects with its own role from the cell's Key Vault, and a write from the AI role to a transactional table is refused by PostgreSQL.

tasks.subject: One id type: UUIDv7 from Id.New() in the kernel and in offline-core
tasks.detail: Replace the kernel's ULID generator (Ticvai.Shared.Kernel Primitives/Ulid.cs) with Id.New(), a UUIDv7 Guid (RFC 9562) written big-endian so PostgreSQL's uuid order is time order (ADR-0056), and the same generator in ticvai-frontend packages/offline-core for ids created offline. Done when: ids made by the server and by an offline till sort by creation time in PostgreSQL, a .NET-to-TypeScript round-trip test agrees byte for byte, and no ULID string is generated anywhere.

tasks.subject: Monthly partitions: create three months ahead, detach what retention has expired
tasks.detail: A job in the workers host that keeps monthly range partitions three months ahead on the time-partitioned tables (access.scan_event, platform.outbox, platform.dead_letter, platform.audit_record, ledger.journal_line, marketing.message_dispatch, kernel.inbox; ADR-0056) in every tenant database, and detaches and archives partitions past their retention (ADR-0047). Done when: a new tenant database has partitions three months ahead, a run with the clock moved forward creates the next month, and an expired partition is detached, not deleted row by row.

tasks.subject: Qdrant cluster in dev and staging: 3 nodes, TLS, snapshots, monitoring
tasks.detail: In **ticvai-infra** (Terraform): a self-hosted 3-node Qdrant cluster in Azure UAE North for dev and staging (ADR-0049), pinned to 1.16 or later, with TLS, JWT RBAC on and the signing key in the cell's Key Vault, snapshot storage in the UAE, and monitoring and alerts on node health, disk and latency. Check Qdrant Hybrid Cloud on our own AKS as an alternative before building. Done when: the cluster survives the loss of one node, a snapshot of a test collection restores into a fresh cluster, and a request without a valid token is refused.

tasks.subject: Offline journal in packages/offline-core: record, replay and the conflict policies
tasks.detail: In ticvai-frontend packages/offline-core: an append-only journal of sales and scans taken offline, replay on reconnect, and the conflict policies the contracts declare (SD-047). Done when: a POS takes ten cash sales with the network off and all ten reach the server once when it returns.

tasks.subject: Signed catalogue and entitlement bundles, and the lease client
tasks.detail: The signed bundle a till or scanner trades from offline, including entitlements and dynamic access policy for the scanner (SD-052), and the lease each workstation holds (SD-047). Done when: a till with an expired lease stops selling offline and says why.

tasks.subject: syncOrders: a result per entry, and a bad entry quarantined instead of blocking the till
tasks.detail: Per-entry outcomes, a quarantine a supervisor resolves, and the till carrying on with the rest (SD-028). Done when: one malformed sale in a batch of twenty is quarantined and the other nineteen are accepted.

tasks.subject: A POS sale reaches the kitchen: routing online, and the LAN path decision
tasks.detail: createFnbOrder from the POS creates the kitchen ticket as the guest order does, routed to the right station (SD-046). The offline LAN path to the Kitchen Display is an ADR decision; this task implements the online path and the stub the decision fills. Done when: a POS sale of a burger and a drink shows on the grill and bar stations. 2 October (Chinmay, DEC-187/189): kitchen printers are in release 1 (print template, printer routing) and routing takes category rules with a default/fallback station per outlet. 8 points (was 5).

tasks.subject: AI gateway, governance decision point and usage metering
tasks.detail: One gateway every AI call goes through: provider (managed Azure by default; BYOK where TICVAI enables it), policy check (evaluateAiGovernance), usage and spend (getAiUsage), and the decision record for every answer. About 10 engineer-days. 2 October (Chinmay, DEC-539): routes each call by the tenant's AI residency class (UAE-only via Core42 Compass by default, Global opt-in under PDPL Art. 23, on-prem open models) and enforces TICVAI's curated model range per task tier (BYOK maps to the provider's equivalent; clients cannot pick models). About 12 engineer-days (was 10).

tasks.subject: Offline PII scrubber and guard model in front of every LLM call
tasks.detail: 2 October (Chinmay, DEC-542/543, ADR-0020 amended): Microsoft Presidio in-cell with UAE recognisers (Emirates ID, UAE phone, passport, IBAN, Luhn-checked cards, email) and Arabic NER for names and places; reversible placeholders whose map stays in-cell and replies re-filled before the user sees them; Qwen3Guard on input and output; fails closed. Mandatory whatever the tenant's residency class. Done when: a prompt with an Emirates ID, an Arabic name and a card number reaches the provider as placeholders and the reply comes back filled. About 6 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: The baseline-then-learn layer: estimator interface, maturity stages, venue profile, starting patterns
tasks.detail: One interface per AI question with three answers behind it (starting pattern, statistical on the tenant's data, trained model); the stage and 'based on' label on every answer; the venue profile entered at onboarding; starting patterns per venue type with the UAE calendar and weather; no other tenant's data. About 15 engineer-days; the rest of the layer continues in Block B.

tasks.subject: Day-one suggestions for the Block A screens: queue balancing, prep plan, upsell
tasks.detail: requestSuggestion answers from the baseline on day one for the kinds Block A screens call (BO-005, GST-031, WEB-044), with the upsell baseline from the Promotions relationship map. About 8 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: Guest concierge: retrieval over the venue's knowledge, answers with sources
tasks.detail: Knowledge ingest and reindex, semantic search, the concierge conversation with the venue's content as its only source, and the answer cache keyed by scope. About 8 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: Qdrant tenancy: a collection and a scoped token per tenant, the retrieval client, erasure and snapshots
tasks.detail: Collection-per-tenant provisioning at tenant onboarding, per embedding model behind the alias tenant_<tenantId> (a model change is a shadow collection and an alias swap); per-tenant JWT issuance and rotation, scoped to the tenant's collections; the single retrieval client with no scope parameter that always adds the venue filter; erasure by guest or document payload, checked against the point references in ai.chunk_embedding; offboarding that deletes the collections and revokes the token; per-collection snapshots (ADR-0049). Done when: a token for one tenant cannot read another tenant's collection, a venue-scoped question never returns another venue's chunk, and an erased guest's points are gone and provably so. About 5 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: Help me choose: suggested question sets from the product catalogue
tasks.detail: proposeGuidedChoice suggests filter questions from product attributes (age and height rules, levels, certifications); the operator edits and publishes, nothing is published automatically. About 4 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: Content translation English and Arabic for the CMS
tasks.detail: proposeTranslations for CMS content, reviewed by the operator before publishing. About 3 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: The planner agent on top of the rules planner
tasks.detail: The agent refines the rules plan by chat, with the plan operations as its tools; when AI is off or fails it falls back to the rules plan, never to an error. About 8 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: Evaluation harness and the promotion alert
tasks.detail: Offline evaluation of every AI answer type against a fixture, the backtest runner the learned producers will use, and the promotion-ready alert to the admin (AI-D16). About 5 engineer-days.

tasks.subject: Per-tenant request budgets: a token bucket per tenant and audience, and a load-aware share per replica
tasks.detail: ADR-0064 (accepted 1 October), in the kernel middleware of the commerce, access and operations hosts: a token bucket per tenant and audience (guest/public, staff, service, partner) with counts shared through Azure Managed Redis, sustained rate and a 2x burst for 10 seconds from the tenant's plan (Plan.requestLimits) or the platform default; one tenant held to 25% of a replica's request slots only while the replica is above 70% of its limit; shedding guest and public first, staff and service last (ADR-0032); 429 with Retry-After and the RateLimit-* headers; if Redis is unavailable each replica falls back to its own in-process buckets (the limit divided by the replica count). Done when: in a test with two tenants on one replica, the busy tenant gets the whole replica while the other is quiet, is held to 25% of the slots once the replica passes 70% while the quiet tenant's requests still succeed, a guest burst never spends a till's staff budget, and stopping Redis leaves requests served under the in-process limits.

tasks.subject: Alerts on one tenant's share of its connection pool and on max_connections
tasks.detail: ADR-0064 item 4: per-tenant pool caps stay, and two alerts watch them: one tenant holding more than 60% of its pool for five minutes, and the instance passing 80% of max_connections; plus a dashboard panel of 429s per tenant and audience from KERNEL-TENANT-LIMITS. Done when: a load run that holds one tenant's pool fires the first alert after five minutes naming the tenant, and opening connections past 80% of max_connections fires the second.

tasks.subject: The on-sale waiting room: Redis positions, the cached page, the release controller, admission tokens
tasks.detail: ADR-0066 (accepted 1 October; B1, or Block A if an on-sale is booked in Block A): enterWaitingRoom gives a position from a Redis counter with no database write; the static branded waiting page is served from Front Door's cache and polls getWaitingRoomPosition; a release controller admits guests per second from the health of commerce (latency and the 429 rate, ADR-0064); an admitted guest gets a short-lived signed token (tenant, performance, expiry, unique id; key in Key Vault) that middleware checks by signature, with no database read, on addCartLine and acquireInventoryHold from guest channels only (till, kiosk and workstation holds are exempt, amendment of 1 October); activation follows the performance's onSaleFrom/onSaleTo or setWaitingRoomSetting. Done when: with the room on, a guest cart hold without a token is refused 403 admission-required, one with a valid token succeeds, a forged or expired token or one for another performance is refused, a till hold needs no token, and the release rate drops when commerce latency rises.

tasks.subject: Load test the waiting room at 30,000 arrivals in the burst environment
tasks.detail: ADR-0066 item 4, before the first large sale: 30,000 arrivals in the opening seconds against a burst environment (ADR-0035) with the waiting room on, recording position latency, the Front Door cache hit rate, the release rate the controller holds, commerce p95 and 429s, and the relay lag while admitted guests buy (ADR-0058 amendment: 3,500 events a second). Done when: all 30,000 get a position without a database write, admitted guests buy with commerce p95 inside its target, no cart hold succeeds without a token, and the results are recorded against the sizing figures.

tasks.subject: One admission rule format, two evaluators: .NET and TypeScript proven equal by shared test vectors
tasks.detail: ADR-0068 (accepted 1 October; B1, with the scanner): the closed JSON rule format (AdmissionRule, AdmissionCondition; conditionRule on access.dynamic_policy versions) evaluated by validateAccess online in .NET and by the gate offline in TypeScript (packages/offline-core) against the same active policy version that getOfflinePackage carries; each scan_event records the policy version that decided it. Done when: one set of test vectors runs in CI against both evaluators and they agree on every vector, a rule the format cannot express is refused when the policy is saved, and an offline scan and an online scan of the same credential under the same policy version give the same decision.

tasks.subject: Identity verification for accreditation: UAE Pass and ICP
tasks.detail: 2 October (Chinmay, DEC-457): UAE Pass sign-in/verification and ICP (Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security) document checks for accreditation applicants, alongside manual review. Needs client access to both (external dependencies register). Done when: an applicant verified through UAE Pass shows the verified identity on the reviewer workspace, and an ICP check result is recorded on the application.

tasks.subject: Same numbers test: till, back-office and Analytics reports agree
tasks.detail: 2 October (Chinmay, DEC-559, prevention of CHG-FIN-006): an automated comparison of the same measure (takings, gross sales, net revenue, refunds) for the same period and scope on the till report (POS-008), the back-office report and the Analytics (P16) dashboard; fails when they differ. Done when: the test runs in CI against the seeded demo tenant.
